prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Production terrain material sheet, Tequila Kill.
Reference image is the approved game concept. Reproduce its ground MATERIALS faithfully, not its buildings or props. Output a wide image divided into exactly TWO EQUAL SQUARE PANELS, left and right, with no gap, no frame, no text or labels. Entire image opaque.
LEFT PANEL: calm warm pale peach-gold desert sand seen vertically from above, like the village plaza in reference. Subtle broad wind-brushed variation, little soft irregular clustered speckles and a few shallow fine tracks. Warm light, soft organic texture, clean crisp pixel-art clusters. Very low contrast so characters remain readable. No stones, bushes, props, objects, paths or shadows.
RIGHT PANEL: cool muted blue-gray saloon floor like reference, seen vertically from above. Long narrow horizontal worn plank-like stone slabs, very fine broken/staggered joints, subtle small color variation and grain, occasional tiny worn marks. Each thin horizontal course spans much of the panel, rows about 12 to 18 pixels high in a 256-square logical tile; no regular square grid. Soft blue-gray material, not bright cyan, not concrete noise. Calm low contrast, gently shaded pixel art. No props, wall edges, doorways, scenery, dramatic shadows or highlights.
Both panels are seamless tileable materials: opposite edges of EACH panel should join quietly. Flat orthographic top view, consistent texture density, no perspective, no bevelled 3D block effect. Keep medium-scale quiet variation, never random high-frequency dithering, no blurring. Use the concept's softly shaded pixel-art surface style.
